assumptions.title: Parallels at their own height
assumptions.assumption: Every parallel is drawn and checked at exactly its nominal height; the part rests where it physically would (on the parallels, on the jaw tops by a flange, or on the table) and its hitbox is checked.
assumptions.source: Owner, item 1 (38 mm parallel drawn above the 45 mm jaws)

assumptions.title: Shape after each operation
assumptions.assumption: The part's outer envelope (holes filled) after every operation is shown per operation and is the hitbox the jaws, parallels and stop touch in the clamping checks.
assumptions.source: Owner, item 2; answer: show it and use as hitbox

assumptions.title: Adjust per clamping
assumptions.assumption: Each clamping has an Adjust toggle with explicit settings: parallels height, Y-, Y+ and X- spacers, side up and turn, previewed live in 3D; the scroll-wheel editing goes.

assumptions.title: One tool at a time
assumptions.assumption: Picking a tool (list, or its path in 3D, highlighted on hover) shows only its path; its row then shows Play (only that tool), Settings and Delete (confirmation; removes its toolpath and tool change).
assumptions.context: CAM AI tool list and simulation

assumptions.title: Free tool swap
assumptions.assumption: Any machine, database or typed tool can replace another; a shape difference only warns; export is blocked only by holder or jaw hits, with CAM AI's choice offered.

assumptions.title: Make again / Undo
assumptions.assumption: After any change a small bar offers Make again and Undo.

assumptions.title: No 2D view in CAM AI
assumptions.assumption: CAM AI's simulation has no 2D view; the remapper's viewer keeps its own.

assumptions.title: Tool database fields
assumptions.assumption: Each tool has an editable type, a role (roughing, finishing or both) and an on/off switch; a program remembers the database tools it used and asks to be made again when one changed.

assumptions.title: Tool choice order
assumptions.assumption: Machine tools first, then the database; with neither, the nearest tool, its operation flagged temporary; export stays allowed with a warning.
assumptions.source: Owner, item 15; answer: allow with a warning

assumptions.title: Import shows the part
assumptions.assumption: The import dialog shows the 3D part beside the choices.

assumptions.title: Measure to the vise
assumptions.assumption: Measuring snaps to the vise bed and the jaw faces as planes.

assumptions.title: The shop vise
assumptions.assumption: Haas HMV-6F: jaws 125 mm long and 45 mm high, checked from the stop face (X = 0) along those 125 mm only; stop 8 mm thick before them.

assumptions.title: CAM AI scope
assumptions.assumption: These 17 items change CAM AI only; the remapper's toolpath viewer stays as it is unless asked.
assumptions.source: Wording of the request (CAM AI screens)

assumptions.title: Deploy rule
assumptions.assumption: Nothing is deployed unless the owner says deploy.

assumptions.title: The 0.5 mm method, always
assumptions.assumption: Clamping 1 cuts the outline and the through holes whole, 0.5 mm under the part (drills at full diameter 0.5 mm past the bottom); after the turn only the face mill takes the rest, plus what only that side reaches. Extra clampings stay for side features. Under that cut a gap down to the jaw tops: 1 mm by default, 1 to 1.5 mm in CAM AI's settings (it was 0.5); the tools keep it over the jaws.

history.reason: Owner: the gap under the outline cut 1 mm, settable 1 to 1.5

assumptions.title: Clamping 1 grip
assumptions.assumption: The jaws grip the stock under the gap (A015): 5 mm wanted (6.5 mm of stock under the part with the 1 mm gap), the designer may go down to 3 mm (4.5 under the part), shown yellow with a warning; less is refused and a thicker Z blank asked for. Never under 3 mm.
assumptions.source: Owner, 2026-11-26 (answered: the 3-4 mm is the jaws' grip)

history.reason: Owner: 5 mm wanted, down to 3 with a warning

assumptions.title: Counterbore on the other face
assumptions.assumption: A through hole whose counterbore opens on the second clamping's face is still made with it, from that side (the earlier rule wins over drilling it in clamping 1).

assumptions.title: Busiest face first
assumptions.assumption: Clamping 1 is the face with the most pockets and holes; after the turn only the face mill, plus anything only that side reaches.

assumptions.title: Blind holes at drawn depth
assumptions.assumption: Only holes through the part get the extra 0.5 mm; blind holes keep the depth on the model.

assumptions.title: Test and deploy rhythm
assumptions.assumption: Test on a few parts, not big runs; deploy after a few tests, run the rest in the background, then push again for the final deploy.

assumptions.title: Always 0.5 mm to face on top
assumptions.assumption: Clamping 1 always faces the top: at least 0.5 mm over the part (but on a white face), so the blank needs 5 mm of extra Z at the least with the 1 mm gap (0.5 over, 4.5 under; 7 mm for the 5 mm grip); less is refused like a thinner blank.

history.reason: The least extra Z follows the 1 mm gap

assumptions.title: Coolant by machine
assumptions.assumption: Coolant is the machine's, on every tool: HAAS-1/5 and FANUC-1/2 coolant, HAAS-2/4 air.

assumptions.title: A drilled hole is not milled again
assumptions.assumption: No end mill in a hole its drill made (no re-milling, no flush bottom, no point cleaning under the part); a counterbore is milled after its smaller hole is drilled; a blind hole open on down in the model is drilled to where it closes (or through).

history.reason: Holes the reader ended early (library run s47)

assumptions.title: Operations in the operator's order
assumptions.assumption: Tools can be reordered per clamping and the program is checked again (the locks are A027).

history.reason: Kept to what the owner stated; the locks split off as A027

assumptions.title: The part turned by quarter turns
assumptions.assumption: OP settings turn the part +/-90 about machine X or Y, adding up, with a green figure of the model; planned exactly so (frames).

assumptions.title: Resting on a step
assumptions.assumption: No unstable rest on a narrow lower step when a wider step can rest on taller parallels; the operator types the thickness where the parallels touch (UNTERLAGE IN EP). CAM AI's own choice is A028.

history.reason: Kept to what the owner stated; CAM AI's choice split off as A028

assumptions.title: Orders that lock
assumptions.assumption: One row per tool; a dragged tool's operations move together, the others keep their places (kept by operation); an order no check covers locks (before the facing, a drill before its spot drill, mills out of their made order, a mill before a drill whose holes it goes into).

history.reason: A drag no longer regroups a tool used in two places

assumptions.title: Resting on a step by itself
assumptions.assumption: Not typed: the deepest step that fits and holds; a quarter turn about Z when the parallels only fit along the jaws (also the operator's face pair, never a hand-turned clamping).
assumptions.source: CAM AI, from the owner's picture and the library's notes

assumptions.title: A tool changed by hand is the operator's call
assumptions.assumption: The accept tick also accepts a part the vise holds off a later zero after a hand tool change; never anything that hits.

assumptions.title: Türkiye tool database: server only, no cutting data
assumptions.assumption: Türkiye's tool database lives only in Türkiye's database, never in the public code: per tool its code, type, Ø, length, radius or angle, flutes, materials and description. The rpm, feeds, step-down and NX file names of the shop's list stay out. Only admins change it (re-importing the list in the app); users only read it.

assumptions.title: Reamers and countersinks
assumptions.assumption: A reamer (RA) is its own type, which the remapper never puts in for a drill call; a 90° countersink (KS) counts as a chamfer tool. SR is a roughing mill, AB with a 118° point a drill, AB 90° a spot drill.

assumptions.title: Adding tools in Türkiye
assumptions.assumption: Türkiye's users add a tool to a machine only from the database: Add new tool opens the next slot (the last slot + 1, or 1), then dropdowns (type, Ø, length, material, ...) narrow each other in any order until one tool is left. Admins can still type a tool the list lacks. The remapper's Add tool (a tool the program needs) picks from the database too, narrowed to the program's Ø. Morocco is unchanged.

history.reason: Owner: the remapper's Add tool picks from the database too

assumptions.title: Türkiye's machines
assumptions.assumption: Türkiye has 17 machines (layout v2): ASB Haas K (50 slots, the probe not counted), Haas M, G, E, F, H (41), Fanuc P, A, C, O, D, B (21); OSB Haas 1, Haas 2 (41), Fanuc 1, 2, 3 (21). The live HAAS F goes from 32 to 41 slots and keeps its tools; the 16 others are added. Done on the owner's deploy.

assumptions.title: The drill for a hole
assumptions.assumption: A hole is drilled with a drill of its own Ø (within 0.015 mm: a drawn Ø2 can read Ø2.01 from the model's facets). Failing that, the nearest smaller drill down to 0.07 mm under it (a Ø2.93 for a Ø3), and that drill's tool says in yellow both sizes, the drill's and the drawing's; a bigger drill within 0.12 mm stays as the engineers drill (Ø3.2 holes with Ø3.3), also marked (Q021). Never a smaller drill and then a mill to bring the hole to size: a hole is milled only when no drill comes that close. Drilling stays first, before the milling (the order rule).
assumptions.source: Owner, 2026-11-27 (an answer on the hole order)

assumptions.title: Peck depth in the plastics
assumptions.assumption: G83 pecks 4 mm in POM, PEEK and PC GF30, at most 4 x the drill's Ø (a Ø0.5 pecks 2), or the engineers' own peck where it is deeper. Aluminium, brass and the laminates (FH, EPO, RESOPAL) keep the engineers' pecks.
assumptions.source: Owner, 2026-11-27 (from an engineer's program: two Ø1 holes with Q4 in POM)

assumptions.title: A slightly bigger drill
assumptions.assumption: With no drill of the hole's Ø, CAM AI still takes one up to 0.12 mm bigger when no smaller one is within 0.07 mm, as the engineers do (Ø3.2 holes with Ø3.3, Ø2.05 with Ø2); its tool says so in yellow. Refuse bigger drills instead (the hole is then milled)?
assumptions.source: A036: the owner named only smaller drills

assumptions.title: 0.1 mm smaller, as the engineers drill
assumptions.assumption: In 3 of the 24 reference parts the engineers drilled holes 0.1 mm under their Ø: Ø5.5 holes with Ø5.4 (two parts), a Ø3.6 hole with Ø3.5. With A036's 0.07 mm limit CAM AI now mills them (about 2 minutes more over the three). Keep 0.07, or allow 0.1 like the engineers?
assumptions.source: Library run s57 against s53 (the engineers' own drills)
